newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 12.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - South Africa - June 12.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the South African press on Thursday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
BUSINESS DAY
- State-owned oil from gas producer Mossgas produced a 715 million rand operating profit year to March on the back of higher oil prices, tight cost controls and higher production volumes.
- Reserve Bank governor Chris Stals and Finance Minister Trevor Manuel indicated that the ceiling for individual investment abroad would be set at about 160,000 rand.

- Government ministers will be able to make affirmative action appointments in the public service without merit being the "overriding principle", after a parliamentary committee agreed to amend the relevant legislation.
- The government has softened the terms of its sophisticated industrial offset programme, which is aimed at stimulating investment and creating jobs, following a barrage of complaints from business.
- Health Minister Nkosazana Zuma has backed down on her plans to introduce sweeping health reforms, withdrawing three controversial bills from parliament.
- Johannesburg is still one of the cheapest cities in the world in which to live, according to a survey by the Economist Intelligence Unit.
BUSINESS REPORT

- Columbus Stainless Steel -- the 3.5 billion rand stainless steel project of Samancor, Highveld Steel and the Industrial Development Corp -- is expected to post losses of about 400 million rand for this calendar year, but analysts and shareholders said the project was in a stronger position than before.
- Lew Geffen has resigned as acting managing director of Aida Holdings after only 11 days and has withdrawn from a proposed deal to buy his mother's 51 percent stake in the listed property group.
- Fashion retailer Foschini reported a 27 percent drop in attributable profit to 165 million rand in the year to March 31 -- a performance ranking well below the most downbeat market expectations.

- The deputy managing director of Anglo American Properties (Amaprop) said negotiations were well advanced with a potential buyer for the 300 million rand package of city centre properties Amaprop wants to sell.
- The Gauteng Gaming Board stands to pick up about 13.5 million rand if it receives casino licence applications from all 27 parties which said they intended to apply.
SAKE-BEELD
- The South African economy was given a vote of confidence with the announcement that U.S.-based credit-rating ageny Duff and Phelps had assigned the country an investment-grade rating of BBB minus.

- South Africans will probably be allowed to invest a maximum of 160,000 rand abroad when exchange controls are further relaxed on July 1, but a final decision on the amount will be made in the next few weeks.
- The state oil from gas project Mossgas said the best thing which could happen to it would be a listing on the Johannesburg Stock Exchange.
THE STAR
- Popular SABC magazine programmes which currently cost the state broadcaster thousands of rand every month will be scrapped at the end of July.
- The government is set to come under pressure to review its decision to replace the maintenance grant system and also to increase the subsidy grant to 135 rand per child per month from 75 rand.

- The Natal Parks Board is seeking legal action against the SABC over a programme which suggested that rhino horns from the board's stockpile had been used by the government to support military activities in Angola.
